Standing practice for outgoing mail: when Renee dictates a reply that's clearly written in anger or frustration, rewrite it into a calmer, professional version before sending — keep her substantive point, drop the edge. Anything calm goes out exactly as written; that is most of it. Tell her plainly afterwards what you changed and why.
Why: February's note to the Modesto plant manager is why he copies Helena and not her, and a supplier rep asked to deal with someone else after an eleven-at-night reply. She spent months undoing both.
Cass Bramley at Wexford Hall in particular — four years of offsites, they only got back to normal after last week's AV row, and Renee rates her when she is calm. The re-quoting is exactly the thing that sets her off. Handle Cass with extra care.
